column1: # More German learner notes, written by Claude (origin "claude"), applied by notes.py: entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
de:doch:particle||As an answer, doch means "yes" after a negative question: "Kommst du nicht?" "Doch!" (Yes, I am coming). In a request it softens or urges: "Komm doch mit!"
de:mal:particle||Mal makes a request softer and friendlier: "Kannst du mal kommen?", "Schau mal!"
de:halt:adverb||Halt (in Switzerland and the south also "eben") means "that's just how it is": "Das ist halt so."
de:noch:adverb|"Noch nicht" means not yet, "nicht mehr" means no longer; "noch ein Bier" means another beer.|
de:dürfen:verb|"Du darfst nicht" means you must not (it is forbidden).|Dürfen asks for permission: "Darf ich hier rauchen?"
de:müssen:verb|"Du musst nicht" means you don't have to, not "you must not" (that is "du darfst nicht").|
de:sollen:verb||Sollen is what someone else wants or expects: "Ich soll morgen anrufen" (I'm supposed to call tomorrow).
de:brauchen:verb|"Du brauchst nicht zu kommen" means you don't need to come (brauchen + zu, usually with nicht or nur).|
de:lassen:verb||Lassen means to let and also to have something done: "Ich lasse mein Velo reparieren" (I'm having my bike repaired).
de:kennenlernen:verb|To meet someone for the first time is kennenlernen, not treffen: "Ich habe sie in Zürich kennengelernt".|
de:schmecken:verb||"Es schmeckt mir" means I like the taste. "Schmeckt's?" is asked at the table.
de:aufhören:verb|"Aufhören mit" + noun, or "aufhören zu" + infinitive: "Hör auf zu rauchen!"|
de:besuchen:verb|Besuchen takes no preposition: "Ich besuche meine Oma". With a place it also means to attend: "eine Schule besuchen".|
de:Frau:noun||Frau means woman, wife and Mrs (Frau Müller). "Meine Frau" is my wife.
de:Herr:noun||Herr means Mr (Herr Meier) and gentleman. Its other forms take -n: "Ich spreche mit Herrn Meier".
de:Kind:noun|"Das Kind" is neuter, also for a girl or boy: "das Kind, es".|
de:weg:adverb|Weg (away, gone) is different from "der Weg" (the way, the path): "Mein Velo ist weg!"|
de:sicher:adjective||Sicher means safe and sure: "Hier bist du sicher" (safe), "Bist du sicher?" (sure).
de:dann:adverb|"Dann" means then (after that); "denn" means because, or adds interest to a question ("Was ist denn los?").|
de:wo:adverb|Wo asks where something is; wohin asks where to, woher where from: "Wohin gehst du?"|
de:ihr:pronoun||Ihr is the plural "you" (ihr seid), and also "her" (ich gebe ihr) and "her/their" (ihr Buch). Ihr with a capital I is the polite "your".
de:sich:pronoun|Many everyday verbs need sich: "sich freuen", "sich setzen", "sich erinnern". "Ich setze mich", not "ich setze".|
de:gleich:adverb||Gleich means right away, soon ("Ich komme gleich") and also the same ("das gleiche Buch").
de:Angst:noun|"Angst haben vor" + dative: "Ich habe Angst vor Hunden".|
de:Hunger:noun|"Ich habe Hunger" (I have hunger), not "ich bin hungrig" in everyday speech; the same with Durst.|
de:ziemlich:adverb||Ziemlich means quite, rather: "ziemlich gut".
de:damals:adverb|"Damals" is back then (a past period); "dann" is then (next).|
de:schaffen:verb||Schaffen meaning "to manage" is weak: schaffte, geschafft ("Ich habe es geschafft!"). Meaning "to create" it is strong: schuf, geschaffen.
de:hängen:verb||Hängen with an object is weak: "Ich habe das Bild an die Wand gehängt." Without one it is strong: "Das Bild hing / hat (CH: ist) an der Wand gehangen."
de:überlegen:verb||"Sich etwas überlegen" means to think something over: "Ich überlege es mir."
de:seit:preposition|For something still going on, German uses seit with the present tense: "Ich wohne seit einem Jahr in Zürich", not "ich habe gewohnt".|
de:wenn:conjunction|For a single event in the past use als, not wenn: "Als ich ankam, regnete es." Wenn is for "if" and for repeated or future "when".|
de:als:conjunction|In comparisons use als: "grösser als", not "grösser wie".|Als is "when" for one event in the past: "Als ich klein war, …"
de:ob:conjunction|"Whether" is ob, not wenn: "Ich weiss nicht, ob er kommt."|
de:bekommen:verb|Bekommen means to get or receive, not "to become" (that is werden): "Ich habe einen Brief bekommen."|
de:also:adverb|Also means "so, therefore", not "also" (that is auch).|
de:Chef:noun|Chef means boss, not cook (a cook is Koch).|
de:sympathisch:adjective|Sympathisch means likeable, nice ("Sie ist mir sympathisch"), not sympathetic (that is mitfühlend).|
de:eventuell:adverb|Eventuell means possibly, maybe, not "eventually" (that is schliesslich).|
de:aktuell:adjective|Aktuell means current, up to date, not "actual" (that is tatsächlich).|
de:Rezept:noun||Rezept is both a recipe and a doctor's prescription.
de:spenden:verb|Spenden means to donate. To spend money is ausgeben; to spend time is verbringen.|
de:ausgeben:verb||Ausgeben means to spend money: "Ich habe zu viel Geld ausgegeben."
de:verbringen:verb||Verbringen means to spend time: "Wir verbringen die Ferien am See."
de:wer:pronoun|Wer means who, not where (that is wo).|
de:Mädchen:noun|"Das Mädchen" is neuter because of the ending -chen: "das Mädchen, es".|
de:groß:adjective||In Switzerland ß is never used: gross, grösser, am grössten.
de:Straße:noun||In Switzerland it is written Strasse: Switzerland does not use ß.
de:schon:adverb||Schon means already, and also reassures: "Das wird schon gehen" (it'll be fine).
de:eigentlich:adverb||Eigentlich means actually, in fact: "Was machst du eigentlich hier?"
de:gern:adverb|To say you like doing something, put gern after the verb: "Ich schwimme gern."|"Ich hätte gern …" is a polite way to order.
de:kosten:verb||Kosten means to cost ("Was kostet das?") and also to taste, to try food.
de:fehlen:verb|To say you miss someone, the person you miss is the subject: "Du fehlst mir" (I miss you).|
de:vermissen:verb||"Ich vermisse dich" means I miss you, the same as "Du fehlst mir".
de:gehören:verb|The owner is in the dative: "Das Buch gehört mir." Belonging to a group is gehören zu.|
de:passen:verb||Passen means to fit or suit ("Das passt mir gut"). In Switzerland "Passt!" also means OK, fine.
de:stimmen:verb||"Das stimmt" means that's right. "Stimmt so!" when paying means keep the change.
de:Rechnung:noun||In a restaurant ask: "Die Rechnung, bitte" (in Switzerland also "Zahlen, bitte").
de:Ferien:noun||In Switzerland Ferien is used for any holiday or vacation; Urlaub sounds more German.
de:Velo:noun||The Swiss word for bicycle (in Germany: Fahrrad).
de:grüezi:interjection||Grüezi is the polite Swiss greeting for people you call Sie; to friends say "Hoi" or "Salü".
de:Sie:pronoun|Use Sie (capital S) with strangers, officials and at work; du with friends, family and children. In Switzerland colleagues often switch to du quickly.|
de:halb:adjective|"Halb drei" means 2:30 (half way to three), not 3:30.|
de:legen:verb|Legen (to put lying down) takes the accusative; liegen (to be lying) the dative: "Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch." "Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch."|
de:stellen:verb|Stellen (to put standing up) takes the accusative; stehen (to be standing) the dative: "Ich stelle die Flasche auf den Tisch."|
de:setzen:verb|Setzen is the action, sitzen the state: "Ich setze mich auf den Stuhl." "Ich sitze auf dem Stuhl."|
de:fast:adverb|Fast means almost, not fast (that is schnell).|
de:bald:adverb||Bald means soon: "Bis bald!" (see you soon).
de:Billett:noun||The Swiss word for a ticket (in Germany: Fahrkarte or Ticket).
de:Spital:noun||The Swiss word for hospital (in Germany: Krankenhaus).
de:parkieren:verb||The Swiss word for to park (in Germany: parken).
de:wohnen:verb|Wohnen is where you live (your home); leben is being alive or how you live: "Ich wohne in Zürich."|
de:lernen:verb|Lernen is to learn or study; to teach is lehren or unterrichten.|"Ich lerne Deutsch."
de:studieren:verb|Studieren is for university studies; for a test or homework say lernen.|
de:bis:preposition||Bis means until or by: "bis Montag", "Bis später!"
de:Buße:noun||In Switzerland it is written Busse and is also the everyday word for a fine: "Ich habe eine Busse bekommen" (I got a fine).
